title: The open–closed triangle at every coefficient stage
statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be
a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary open
immersion. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient stages
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, with the categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$
([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]), the pullbacks $i^*,j^*$ of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the direct image $i_*=Ri_*$ of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the extension by zero $j_!=Rj_!$ of
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ the open counit and the closed unit extend to a
distinguished triangle, the open–closed recollement triangle of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement],
$$
j_!j^*K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow i_*i^*K
\longrightarrow j_!j^*K[1].
$$
Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*K[m],i_*i^*K)=0$ for all $m$; hence the
third arrow is uniquely determined by the other two and the triangle is
functorial in $K$. If $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, $Z$, $U$ come from
$k_0$-schemes, $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and $K$ is a Weil complex
([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]), then all three arrows are
Weil-equivariant.

proof.text: The schemes in the statement are Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0$ and $(1)$, so its spectrum is Noetherian, and apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Here $Z$ is finite type over $k$: intersect a finite affine finite-type cover of $X$ with $Z$ and take quotient coordinate rings. The open $U$ is also finite type over $k$: each of its intersections with those Noetherian affines is quasi-compact, hence a finite union of principal opens, whose rings are finitely generated over $k$ by adjoining an inverse. Every open in a Noetherian affine is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so $j$ is quasi-compact. We will use the ringed sheaf sequence with this hypothesis. At finite coefficients, inverse image along $i$ or $j$ preserves constructibility: intersect a finite locally closed constructible partition with $Z$ or $U$, and restrict the locally constant finite modules. Extension by zero along $j$ preserves constructibility: use the partition on $U$, viewed in $X$, together with $Z$, on which the restriction is zero. Direct image along $i$ preserves constructibility: view the partition of $Z$ in $X$ and add $U$, using $i^{-1}i_* = \mathrm{id}$ and $j^{-1}i_*=0$. These identities and exactness of $j_!,i_*$ are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]; exactness of inverse images is [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Thus each functor preserves the cohomological interval of a bounded finite-coefficient complex, since exact functors commute with kernels, images and cokernels. The partition condition is exactly [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

source.place: Finite stage: quasi-compactness and constructible vertices; unit proof, exact sheaf sequence.

proof.text: At finite coefficients apply the counit--unit short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to every term of a representative complex of $K$. The maps are natural in the sheaf, hence commute with the differentials. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] this short exact sequence of complexes gives a distinguished triangle $j_!j^{-1}K\to K\to i_*i^{-1}K\to j_!j^{-1}K[1]$. The exact functors induce triangulated functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], and their ordinary derived functors are their termwise functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Thus the vertices and first two maps are exactly those in the statement. Step 1 puts the triangle in the full bounded constructible subcategory. This is the unit's termwise sheaf-sequence argument, with the ringed pro-etale sequence supplying the sheaf calculation; it does not assume ordinary geometric stalks conservative on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: Finite stage: the exact sequence and its derived triangle; unit proof.

proof.text: For the integral stage put $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$ and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] the actual inverse-image coefficient sheaves for $i,j$ are $R_Z,R_U$, compatibly with all finite quotient maps. Write $I=i^{-1}$, $J=j^{-1}$, $H=i_*$ and $L=j_!$ for the ordinary module functors for these ring sheaves. They satisfy the exact sequence, adjunctions, exactness and support identities of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], $I,J$ are exact and preserve countable products. On derived categories these products are represented termwise by [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], since products of pro-etale module sheaves are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Consequently $I,J$ carry a Roos triangle to a Roos triangle by [lem-pc-homotopy-limit-map]. Applied to the reduction tower of an integral $K$, this identifies $IK,JK$ with the completed pullbacks defined in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Indeed inverse image commutes with restriction of the module action along $R_T\to(A_n)_T$ by the compatible ring identifications, and the image tower is exactly $(\operatorname{Res}_n i_n^*K_n)_n$ or $(\operatorname{Res}_n j_n^*K_n)_n$, including its transition maps. The identifications commute with the projections and maps from $K$.

source.place: Integral stage: identify ordinary immersion restriction with completed pullback.

proof.text: The functor $L$ also preserves countable products. Here is the argument, rather than a new lemma. For a module $N$ on $U$, $Jj_*N=N$: in the slice-site description, restriction of $V\mapsto N(V\times_X U)$ back to $U$ evaluates $N$ on the same objects. Apply the ringed sheaf sequence to $j_*N$ to get $LN=\ker(j_*N\to HIj_*N)$. Both $j_*$ and $H$ preserve products as right adjoints (the adjunction and the universal property of a product give $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,R\prod N_a)=\prod_a\operatorname{Hom}(Q,RN_a)$); $I$ preserves products by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. Taking the kernel of the product diagram gives the product of the kernels. Thus $L\prod N_a=\prod LN_a$. This is the proof of Stacks Tag 09BP, label lemma-j-shriek-limits, from the cited sheaf sequence and limit preservation. Exactness of $L$ and the termwise description of derived products now let [lem-pc-homotopy-limit-map] apply to $L$ too.

source.place: Tag 09BP, label lemma-j-shriek-limits: kernel proof of product preservation.

proof.text: The ordinary $L$ commutes with derived reduction, including quotient transitions. To check it explicitly, take a K-flat representative $P$ of $N$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] extends to total tensor complexes: $F\otimes LP=L(JF\otimes P)$, since $L$ preserves direct sums as a left adjoint [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. If $F$ is acyclic, then $JF$ is acyclic; K-flatness of $P$ and exactness of $L$ show $LP$ is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Hence $(LN)\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ is represented by $(LP)\otimes_{R_X}(A_n)_X=L(P\otimes_{R_U}(A_n)_U)$, which is $L_n(N\otimes^L_{R_U}(A_n)_U)$. On underlying module presheaves changing the scalar action and extending by zero commute: on objects factoring through $U$ both are the same module with the same action, and on the other objects both are zero; the same universal property of module sheafification gives the sheaf comparison. This identifies the displayed right side with the finite-coefficient extension $L_n$. Every comparison is tensor balancing and respects $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, so these are comparisons of towers, not merely separate isomorphisms.

source.place: Integral stage: explicit reduction comparison for extension by zero; ringed slice tensor argument.

proof.text: For integral $N$, steps 4--5 carry its defining Roos triangle to one for $LN$ with its actual finite reductions and their maps from $LN$. Thus $LN$ is derived complete by [def-weil-derived-complete]. Its reductions are the finite extensions $L_nN_n$, whose constructibility and common cohomological interval follow from step 1. Hence $LN\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and $LN=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nL_nN_n$ is exactly the integral $Rj_!N$ of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], using the compactification $U\xrightarrow{j}X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X$. For integral $M$ on $Z$, apply [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] to its reduction tower and the closed direct image. Its tower comparison identifies ordinary $Ri_*M$ with the derived limit of the finite direct images; its completeness clause makes this object derived complete; and its projection-formula clause identifies each reduction with $Ri_{*,n}M_n$, compatibly with $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Since $i_*$ is exact, ordinary $Ri_*$ is $H$ applied termwise. Step 1 gives a common interval for its reductions, so $HM$ belongs to the integral constructible category and agrees with [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. The integral pullbacks preserve the constructible category and have the asserted reductions by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible].

source.place: Integral stage: completeness, uniform amplitude, and identification of the compact-support and ordinary direct images.

proof.text: For a representative complex $B^\bullet$ of the integral $K$, the ringed localization sequence in each degree gives $0\to LJB^q\to B^q\to HIB^q\to0$. Naturality of the counit and unit makes these maps commute with $d^q$, so this is a short exact sequence of complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Steps 3 and 6 identify all three vertices with $j_!j^*K,K,Ri_*i^*K$ in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. This category has the induced triangles by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. The maps are the ordinary open counit and closed unit. The open exact adjunction descends to the derived categories by [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived], since exact functors are their absolute derived functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]; the closed derived adjunction is [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The preceding tower identifications are induced by the same sheaf maps, so this is also the pair of maps for the completed operations. In particular the reductions of these maps are the finite maps; their compatibility with units and counits is also stated in [lem-fix-operation-reduction].

source.place: Integral stage: the triangle of the termwise sheaf sequence and its specified arrows.

proof.text: At both finite and integral stages the stronger cross-object vanishing holds: for any $N\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$, $M\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N[m],i_*M)=\operatorname{Hom}(N[m],j^*i_*M)=0$. The adjunction comes from the exact ringed sheaf adjunction by [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], and $j^*i_*=0$ is the exact support identity of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applied termwise. At integral coefficients steps 3 and 6 justify using these ordinary operations for the completed symbols. Taking $N=j^*K$ and $M=i^*K$ gives the required vanishing.

source.place: Finite and integral Hom vanishing, with different source and target objects allowed.

proof.text: Here is the uniqueness and naturality argument used at every stage below. Write $A_K=j_!j^*K$ and $C_K=i_*i^*K$, and assume the cross-object vanishing of step 8. For two completions of the same pair $A_K\to K\to C_K$, TR3 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] supplies $(1,1,h)$ between their triangles. The second square gives $(h-1)v=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact](ii), $h-1=t\delta$ for some $t:A_K[1]\to C_K$. Vanishing gives $t=0$, hence $h=1$; the third square then says the connecting maps coincide. For $f:K\to K'$, TR3 applied to $(j_!j^*f,f)$ produces a third component $h$. Naturality of the closed unit implies $(h-i_*i^*f)v=0$. The same factorization gives a map $A_K[1]\to C_{K'}$, zero by cross-object vanishing, so $h=i_*i^*f$. The third square is exactly naturality of the connecting arrow. This corrects the imported phrase 'hence through a zero map': it is $t$ that is zero, and $\delta:C_K\to A_K[1]$ need not be zero.

source.place: Finite-stage last sentence and functoriality: explicit TR3 and Hom-exactness argument.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] uses raw scalar localization with the same objects and Hom groups $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_E}(-,-)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, and its localization functor is exact. The operations and maps are the rationalized integral ones; [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] extends exact linear functors and their transformations, and [lem-fix-operation-reduction] includes the compatibility of these operations, units and counits with rationalization. Applying localization to the integral triangle gives the required triangle. Every cross-object Hom group of step 8 becomes $0\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E=0$. Step 9 proves uniqueness and naturality also for arbitrary rational morphisms, which need not be integral morphisms.

source.place: Rational stage: raw scalar localization and transported maps.

proof.text: The schemes $X,U,Z$ are Noetherian by step 1 and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], applied to their finite-type structure morphisms over $k$; the coefficient datum has $\ell\ne p=\operatorname{char}k$, so $\ell$ is invertible on all three. These verify the scheme hypotheses of the scalar-extension theorem. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, choose a finite stage $(E,K)$ as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Scalar extension is exact with the coherent comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]; compatibility for compact support as well as pullback and direct image, including units and counits, is [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Consequently [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] descends the four functors and the two transformations, with the same interpretation of compact support as [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The $E$-triangle maps to a distinguished triangle, because finite-stage inclusions are exact [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms]. For possibly different finite stages $N,M$, represent both over a common extension $L$. At every further stage the group $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N_L[m],i_*M_L)$ is zero by step 10. The common-stage Hom formula in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] is a filtered colimit of these zero groups, and is zero. Step 9 again proves uniqueness and functoriality, now for every common-stage morphism.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: common-stage triangles, maps, and Hom groups.

proof.text: Finally let $g_X,g_U,g_Z$ be the geometric Frobenius automorphisms of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Because $i,j$ and the schemes are defined over $k_0$, these automorphisms commute with the immersions. They may be semilinear over $k$, so we use [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] directly: pullback along each $g_T$ and $g_T^{-1}$ gives inverse equivalences of pro-etale sites preserving covering families. The coefficient identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] respect composites and finite projections. Hence the induced module pullbacks are inverse exact equivalences; they preserve finite constructibility partitions and the Roos triangles for completeness, and therefore induce the Frobenius pullbacks $F_T=g_T^*$ on all four coefficient categories.

source.place: Weil structures: semilinear site equivalences and coefficient compatibility.

proof.text: Composition of these base-change functors gives $b:F_Uj^*\cong j^*F_X$ and $d:F_Zi^*\cong i^*F_X$. Define $c:F_Xi_*\cong i_*F_Z$ as the right-adjoint mate of $d^{-1}:i^*F_X\cong F_Zi^*$, and define $a:F_Xj_!\cong j_!F_U$ as the inverse of the left-adjoint conjugate $j_!F_U\to F_Xj_!$ of $b$. The vertical functors are equivalences, so [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] makes the right-adjoint mate an isomorphism; applying the same result to opposite adjunctions makes the left-adjoint conjugate an isomorphism. These constructions are made first on module sheaves and then termwise on complexes and through the completed, rational and common-stage models of steps 3--7 and 10--11; no $k$-linearity of $g_T$ is used.

source.place: Weil structures: construction and invertibility of the Frobenius mate comparisons.

proof.text:
The mate formulas are compatible with the units and counits. The unit and counit identities in [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] and [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit], together with the pasting and identity laws of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], give componentwise
$$F_X\varepsilon_K=\varepsilon_{F_XK}\circ j_!(b_K)\circ a_{j^*K},\qquad i_*(d_K)\circ c_{i^*K}\circ F_X\eta_K=\eta_{F_XK}.$$
Thus these are the actual mate equations, rather than an appeal to a $k$-linear exchange theorem.

source.place: Weil structures: explicit mate equations for the open counit and closed unit.

proof.text:
If $\theta:F_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ is the Weil structure of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], define structures on the outer terms by
$$\theta_A=j_!j^*(\theta)\circ j_!(b_K)\circ a_{j^*K},\qquad \theta_C=i_*i^*(\theta)\circ i_*(d_K)\circ c_{i^*K}.$$
The two mate equations of step 14 and naturality of the unit and counit give $\varepsilon_K\theta_A=\theta F_X\varepsilon_K$ and $\eta_K\theta=\theta_CF_X\eta_K$. Since $F_X$ is an exact equivalence, it transports the distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle with these same first two arrows under $\theta_A,\theta,\theta_C$, using the stagewise triangulation supplied by [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms].

source.place: Weil structures: induced Weil structures on the outer terms and transport of the triangle.

proof.text:
Apply the uniqueness argument of step 9 to the original triangle and the transported triangle: the first two squares already commute, and the factorization through the connecting morphism is killed by the cross-object Hom vanishing. Equivalently, the uniqueness calculation using [def-weil-triangulated-category] and [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] forces the third square
$$\delta_K\theta_C=\theta_A[1]F_X(\delta_K),$$
with the canonical shift comparison. Therefore all three arrows are Weil-equivariant in the category of pairs; no triangulated structure on that category is asserted.

source.place: Weil structures: uniqueness of the connecting arrow and equivariance of the third map.
